newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH HEALTH MINISTER SURVIVES CONFIDENCE VOTE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH HEALTH MINISTER SURVIVES CONFIDENCE VOTE.

text.p: Poland's parliament on Friday overwhelmingly rejected a motion of no-confidence in health minister Ryszard Zochowski, whom the opposition accuses of bad management and allowing the waste of scarce resources.
Only 77 deputies backed the motion tabled by the centrist opposition Union for Freedom (UW), while 252 rejected it and 41 abstained from voting.
The health ministry has been troubled by almost a year of strikes and protests by doctors over pay and has also been at the centre of controversy over hospital procurement practices.

The government watchdog, the Supreme Auditing Chamber (NIK) in February reported that 60 or more hospitals had been buying medical equipment they could not afford in their budgets and their debts were then sold on to other firms.

These firms waited for interest to build up and used the inflated debts to settle tax bills under a government scheme designed to help debt-ridden public institutions. The practice, known as debt-breeding, cost at least $33 million, NIK said.
Zochowski has argued that most of such abuses took place in hospitals run by provincial governments and not his ministry and that he had stepped in to halt such abuses.
Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz, like medical doctor Zochowski a member of the dominant ex-communist grouping in Poland's ruling coalition, defended him as an able reformer.

"Above all Jacek Zochowski is an energetic proponent of reforms in the health service which is bringing about a rationalisation of public spending," Cimoszewicz said on Thursday during a parliamentary debate on the motion.

Poland's National Union of Doctors this week decided to stop issuing sick-leave certificates to patients, a move designed to complicate government administration, in the latest form of protest to demand higher pay and funding for health.
